the availability of phosphorus from plant sources is influenced by steam pelleting.

1) Steam pelleting increases the availability of phosphorus from plant sources to laying hens, 2) This increased availability is not due to an increased solubility of phytate, 3) The increased availability is due to a change in phytate metabolism, 4) The change is due to the action of phytases, 5) The phytases are produced by the intestinal bacteria of the laying hen and, 6) Steam pelleting enhances the
The influence of steam pelleted diets on the utilization of dietary phosphates by laying hens.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of steam pelletting on phosphorus utilization by the laying hen, the influence of dietary phosphorus level on egg weight and shell quality, and the influence of dietary calcium on the utilization of dietary phosphor-us.
the effect of steam pelleting upon the utilization of plant phosphorus by the hen and the mechanism by which this effect is produced.
the effect of steam pelleting and the use of a pelleting aid on the utilization of dietary phosphorous.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steam pelleting process does not influence the availability of plant origin phosphorus to the laying hen.
steam pelleting does increase the utilization of phosphates of plant origin.
the utilization of phosphorous from a plant source was increased by steam pelleting and that the increase was dependent on the level of calcium in the diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

pelleting does not enhance the utilization of phosphorous from plant sources in a laying hen ration, and that the availability of phosphorus from plant sources is not significantly affected by the addition of 1% of a commercial enzyme preparation.
the steam pelleting of a laying hen ration containing 0.5% of plant phosphorus increased the availability to 70%.

the availability of phytate phosphorus to the laying hen is increased by the steam pelleting process and that the degree of increase is dependent on the level of phytate present in the diet and the length of time the pelleted diets were stored.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the steam peeling process is not the only factor that influences the availability of plant P.
the pelleting process can enhance the utilization of phosphates from plant origin in poultry diets.
we can’t just rely on the current methods to measure the availability of phosphorus in feedstuffs.
